subject: Post-call recap & recommended deployment path: Hosted vs Dedicated
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jen Simmons <jen.simmons@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & recommended deployment path: Hosted vs Dedicated

Jen — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery plus an initial recommendation so your team can move toward a decision.

What we heard (requirements summary):
- Latency: p95 inference latency target <= 120 ms for a ~512-token prompt/response mix (interactive clinician workflow).
- Throughput: sustained ~200 requests/sec with peaks up to ~500 requests/sec during morning triage windows.
- Data & isolation: PHI-sensitive; customer prefers not to have any persistent training data in shared tenancy.
- Ops: want predictable SLAs and a clear path to capacity commitments; prefer fast failover in case of regional issues.

Initial evaluation:
- Hosted API: fastest path to production (no infra to run), but for a p95 <= 120 ms at sustained 200 RPS with 500 RPS peaks we expect variable queuing depending on model choice. Works well if you accept modest latency variance and prefer OPEX/managed tradeoffs.
- Dedicated capacity: recommended if you prioritize predictable p95 under sustained load. Dedicated GPU pools will give you pinned concurrency, consistent kernel selection and lower variance. Also easier to configure autoscale/burst policies to handle the 500 RPS peaks while keeping p95 SLAs.
- Private/VPC: viable if you also require on-prem or air-gapped. Separate procurement track.

Next immediate ask: please share a 48-72h sample of request timestamps (CSV) or expected hourly traffic matrix and the model family you plan to run (e.g., LlamaX-13B-q4, Mistral-7B, etc.). With that we can: (a) run a sizing calc, (b) produce a cost delta Hosted vs Dedicated, and (c) propose an autoscale profile.

Attachments: I attached a simple calculator and a starter mutual action plan that maps milestones -> owners -> dates.

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- You: share traffic sample & preferred model by Wed 04/01.
- Our SE (Vivek): will return a Dedicated sizing + expected p95 estimate by Fri 04/03.
- Joint: 30-minute deep-dive on Fri to walk the sizing and expected cost delta.

If you'd like a short demo showing how Dedicated autoscale + fallback to Hosted looks in the Console, we can do that in the same session.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-hosted-calculator.xlsx, mutual-action-plan-aurelia.docx

From: Jen Simmons <jen.simmons@aureliahealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aureliahealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & recommended deployment path: Hosted vs Dedicated

Thanks Sean — clear summary. A few clarifying questions before we pull our traffic slice:  
1) For Dedicated, what is the expected cold-start behavior during autoscale events? We need near-instant capacity for a sudden 10x burst for severe weather events.
2) Can Dedicated automatically fallback to Hosted in the event of regional capacity exhaustion? We want failover without code changes.
3) Any constraints on model family support for the kernels you mentioned (we are evaluating one ~13B and one ~34B variant).

We’ll try to share the sample traffic matrix by EOD Wed. Also please include rough ballpark TCO delta (per-Month) so we can flag budget.

—Jen
Jen Simmons
Director, Digital Care Platforms | Aurelia Health
jen.simmons@aureliahealth.com | +1 617-555-4426

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jen Simmons <jen.simmons@aureliahealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & recommended deployment path: Hosted vs Dedicated

Jen — short answers and what we’ll include in the sizing pack:  
1) Cold-starts: Dedicated pools keep hot model instances; autoscale actions allocate additional GPU nodes which typically start serving within 60–180s depending on model size (13B vs 34B). For sub-20s scale-up you’ll want a configured burst pool (warm standby nodes) — we can size that for rare 10x bursts (incurs standby cost but gives fast headroom).
2) Fallback to Hosted: Yes — we support policy-based routing to fallback to compatible Hosted variants. That path preserves availability but may change latency/cost; we’ll include expected delta and transparent headers so you can measure fallbacks.
3) Model family constraints: 13B class models generally map to optimized kernels with lower memory foot‑print and faster p95; 34B often requires multi-GPU or higher memory nodes and increases p95 by ~30–60% under identical load. We’ll call out specific kernel footprints in the report.

What I’ll deliver once we have traffic CSV:
- Node/pool count for Dedicated (steady + burst standby) and expected p95 for your target prompt length.
- Cost comparison (Hosted OPEX vs Dedicated committed + standby).
- Autoscale policy proposal (thresholds, cooldowns, pre-warming rules).

I attached a first-pass calculator with sample inputs (Sean included it) — I’ll update with your traffic and model choice.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & recommended deployment path: Hosted vs Dedicated

Jen — great, appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple operational items to lock in so we don’t slow procurement:  
- Action: Aurelia to provide 48–72h request timestamps or the expected hour-by-hour traffic matrix. Owner: Jen. Due: EOD Wed 04/01 (noted).
- Action: Redwood SE (Vivek) to deliver Dedicated sizing + p95 estimate + cost delta. Owner: Vivek. Due: Fri 04/03.
- Action: Schedule 30-min review (Sean + Vivek + Jen + Aurelia procurement). Sean will send calendar invite for Fri 04/03 10:00 AM PT unless you prefer a different slot.

Notes on decision drivers: if Aurelia requires strict p95 <= 120 ms under sustained 200 RPS, Dedicated + burst standby is the conservative path. If you can tolerate occasional p95 variance and prefer no upfront commits, Hosted with an SLA add-on may be sufficient for initial rollout and is faster to sign.

If procurement wants a templated statement-of-work and a Dedicated commit scenario for legal to review, I can draft a short exhibit to attach to the order form.

Thanks — sending the calendar now.

Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Onward: calendar invite link and the updated calc will follow in separate email.
